intent_en: To explain how public health responses aim to keep infection rates below healthcare capacity to ensure treatment availability and prevent hospital overload.
previous_intent: To demonstrate the rationale for epidemic response measures, specifically to keep infection rates below healthcare capacity so that all patients can receive treatment and hospitals are not overwhelmed.
narration_support: so that everyone who gets sick can get treatment and there's no crunch point with overwhelmed hospitals.
chart_support: Area chart plotting Infections against Time, showing the infection curve remaining below a horizontal threshold line.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly states the goal of avoiding overwhelmed hospitals and ensuring treatment, while the chart visualizes the 'flattening the curve' concept where the infection rate (curve) stays below a capacity limit (horizontal line) over time.
